newsitem.title: UK: U.S. announces $10 million in food aid to N. Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. announces $10 million in food aid to N. Korea.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday formally announced an extra $10 million in food aid for North Korea, considerably more than originally expected and above last year's donation of $6.4 million.
But the aid -- amounting to about 100,000 tons of commodities -- still falls way short of internationally recognised needs, judged by aid agencies to be upwards of 2.3 million tons of commodities.
"The U.S. government will provide corn soy blend for children under age five as well as rice and corn for flood victims," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a writen statement.

"The United States has chosen the WFP (World Food Program) as the channel for this assistance because of the WFP's proven ability to monitor distribution to ensure that aid reaches those in need," he said.

U.S. officials have said publicly for two weeks that Washington would respond positively to a new request from the World Food Programme, a United Nations agency. Officials said the announcement was not related to the recent defection of a top North Korean official to the South Korean embassy in Beijing.
Burns said flooding in North Korea in 1995 and 1996 destroyed considerable farmland and exacerbated the Stalinist country's chronic food production shortfalls.
South Korea was expected to offer roughly an extra $5 million in food aid, U.S. officials have said.
The World Food Programme, a U.N. agency, last week issued an appeal for $41.6 million in new food aid for North Korea.
Washington last year contributed about $6.4 million in food aid to North Korea.
